docs.title: confluence-markdown
docs.text:
Proof of Concept — This tool is experimental. No guarantee of correctness or stability.

A Python CLI tool for reading, editing, and managing Confluence Data Center pages in Markdown format.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Read and download Confluence pages as Markdown
  • Edit pages in your preferred editor (vim, VS Code, nano, …)
  • Add content to existing pages (Markdown or HTML)
  • Create new pages and task pages
  • Interactive page selection with fzf or InquirerPy
  • Search pages by full-text or CQL query
  • Recursive batch download of entire page trees
  • Response caching for faster repeated access
  • Multiple configuration profiles, per-space settings
  • Secrets stored securely in the system keychain (macOS)
  • Shell tab completion (bash/zsh)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: uv tool install git+https://github.com/jvanvinkenroye/confluence_markdown.git

docs.title: 1. Set up configuration
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action config set
# Base URL: https://confluence.example.com
# Username: myuser
# Token: ****

docs.title: 2. Test authentication
docs.text: confluence-markdown --action config test --config

docs.title: 3. Browse recent pages
docs.text: confluence-markdown --action read-recent --config

docs.title: 4. Edit a page
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action edit --config \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: uv tool install git+https://github.com/jvanvinkenroye/confluence_markdown.git

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Three authentication methods are supported:

docs.title: Personal Access Token (recommended)
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --base-url https://confluence.example.com \
  --username myuser \
  --token MY_TOKEN \
  --action test-auth

docs.title: Username + Password
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --base-url https://confluence.example.com \
  --username myuser \
  --password mypassword \
  --action test-auth

docs.title: Bearer Token (OAuth)
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --base-url https://confluence.example.com \
  --token MY_BEARER_TOKEN \
  --action test-auth

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Credentials can be saved so they don't need to be provided on every call. Secrets (token, password) are stored in the system keychain (macOS Keychain) — not as plaintext.

docs.title: Initial setup
docs.text:
Interactive (recommended):

confluence-markdown --action config set
# Base URL: https://confluence.example.com
# Username: myuser
# Token: ****

With flags (for scripting):

confluence-markdown --action config set \
  --base-url https://confluence.example.com \
  --username myuser \
  --token MY_TOKEN

docs.title: Show current configuration
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action config show
# Profile: default
#   base_url: https://confluence.example.com
#   username: myuser
#   token: ****

Show a different profile:

confluence-markdown --action config show --profile work

docs.title: List all profiles
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action config list
# Available profiles:
#   - default (base_url: https://confluence.example.com)
#   - work    (base_url: https://work.confluence.com)

docs.title: Delete a profile
docs.text: confluence-markdown --action config delete --profile work

docs.title: Test authentication
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action config test --config
# Authentication successful!
#    User: John Doe
#    Username: myuser

docs.title: Multiple profiles
docs.text:
Profiles allow using different Confluence instances or accounts:

# Create a second profile
confluence-markdown --action config set \
  --base-url https://work.confluence.com \
  --username workuser \
  --token WORK_TOKEN \
  --profile work

# Use a profile
confluence-markdown --action read --config --profile work \
  "https://work.confluence.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Per-space configuration
docs.text:
Edit ~/.config/confluence-markdown/config.json to set per-space defaults:

{
  "default": {
    "base_url": "https://confluence.example.com",
    "username": "myuser",
    "token_in_keychain": true,
    "editor": "vim",
    "table_format": "markdown",
    "spaces": {
      "DOCS": { "editor": "code", "table_format": "yaml" },
      "WIKI": { "editor": "nano" }
    }
  }
}

Config file location: ~/.config/confluence-markdown/config.json Permissions are automatically set to 600. Token and password are stored in the keychain.

docs.title: Read a single page
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action read --config \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

Raw Markdown output (no Rich rendering):

confluence-markdown --action read --config --raw \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

Save to file:

confluence-markdown --action read --config \
  --output page.md \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Browse recently viewed pages (interactive)
docs.text:
Opens an interactive selector of recently viewed pages:

confluence-markdown --action read-recent --config

Adjust the number of pages shown:

confluence-markdown --action read-recent --config --limit 20

Without fzf (InquirerPy fallback):

confluence-markdown --action read-recent --config --no-fzf

docs.title: Open a page in the editor
docs.text:
Opens the page in the configured editor ($EDITOR, default: nvim):

confluence-markdown --action edit --config \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

Use a specific editor:

confluence-markdown --action edit --config --editor code \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

Edit tables in YAML format (easier for complex tables):

confluence-markdown --action edit --config --table-format yaml \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Non-interactive editing (scripting)
docs.text:
With --content, the editor is skipped — the provided content is uploaded directly:

confluence-markdown --action edit --config \
  --content "## New Section

This content was added automatically." \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

Content from a file:

confluence-markdown --action edit --config \
  --content "$(cat my-page.md)" \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

Upload HTML content:

confluence-markdown --action edit --config \
  --content "<h2>Title</h2><p>Text</p>" \
  --content-type html \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Edit recently modified pages (interactive)
docs.text: confluence-markdown --action edit-recent --config

docs.title: Add content (append / prepend)
docs.text:
Append content to an existing page:

confluence-markdown --action add --config \
  --content "## Appendix

This text was appended." \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

Prepend content:

confluence-markdown --action add --config \
  --prepend \
  --content "## Notice

This page is outdated." \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Fully interactive (recommended)
docs.text:
When --space and --parent-id are omitted, the tool guides you interactively:

  1. Space selection — fzf list of all available spaces
  2. Parent page selection — choose one of:
  3. No parent — page is created at root level
  4. Search in space — all pages in the space loaded into fzf for fuzzy search
  5. Pick from recent pages — last 20 modified pages in fzf
# Fully interactive: select space, parent, then edit in editor
confluence-markdown --action create-edit

# Space known, parent interactive
confluence-markdown --action create-edit --space MYSPACE

docs.title: Non-interactive (scripting)
docs.text:
Provide all parameters to skip every prompt:

confluence-markdown --action create \
  --space MYSPACE \
  --title "New Page" \
  --content "## Introduction

This is the content of the new page."

As a child of a known page:

confluence-markdown --action create \
  --space MYSPACE \
  --title "Child Page" \
  --parent-id 12345 \
  --content "## Content"

docs.title: Create a page in the editor
docs.text:
Opens the editor with a template — title is taken from the first # heading:

# Fully interactive
confluence-markdown --action create-edit

# With pre-filled title
confluence-markdown --action create-edit --space MYSPACE --title "Draft: New Page"

docs.title: Create a task page
docs.text:
Creates a structured task page (specific format for task tracking):

confluence-markdown --action create-task --config \
  --parent-id 12345 \
  --title "XWiki Migration" \
  --category "Tools" \
  --priority 80 \
  --status offen \
  --content "Task description"

Priority: 100 = very high, 80 = high, 50 = medium, 0 = low Status: offen, in Arbeit, erledigt, Backlog, wont do

docs.title: Full-text search
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action search --config --query "Confluence Migration"

Limit the number of results:

confluence-markdown --action search --config --query "Meeting Notes" --limit 20

docs.title: CQL search (Confluence Query Language)
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action search --config \
  --cql "space = MYSPACE AND title ~ 'Meeting' ORDER BY lastmodified DESC"

Pages by current user:

confluence-markdown --action search --config \
  --cql "creator = currentUser() ORDER BY created DESC" \
  --limit 10

docs.title: Download a single page
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action download --config \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

To a specific file:

confluence-markdown --action download --config \
  --output page.md \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Download a page and all child pages
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action download --config \
  --recursive \
  --output-dir ./export \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

All files are saved as <page-title>.md in the target directory.

docs.title: Direct children only
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action list-children --config \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: All descendants recursively (parallel)
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action list-children --config \
  --recursive \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text: Option Description --config Load credentials from saved profile --profile NAME Select profile (default: default) --base-url URL Confluence base URL --username USER Username --token TOKEN Personal Access Token --password PASS Password --raw Output raw Markdown (no Rich rendering) --width N Override output width for Rich rendering --verbose Enable verbose debug output --quiet / -q Suppress informational messages (for scripting) --no-fzf Disable fzf, use InquirerPy instead --no-cache Disable response cache --clear-cache Clear cache and exit --editor PROG Editor for edit actions (e.g. vim, nano, code) --table-format Table format when editing: markdown or yaml --limit N Number of results (default: 10)

docs.title: Bash
docs.text:
# Add to ~/.bashrc:
eval "$(register-python-argcomplete confluence-markdown)"

Or with --completion:

confluence-markdown --completion bash >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

docs.title: Zsh
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --completion zsh >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

docs.title: Quiet mode for scripting
docs.text:
# Output only the page URL, suppress INFO messages
confluence-markdown --action add --config --quiet \
  --content "Automated entry" \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"

docs.title: Replace page content from a script
docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PAGE_URL="https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"
CONTENT=$(./generate_report.py)

confluence-markdown --action edit --config --quiet \
  --content "$CONTENT" \
  "$PAGE_URL"

docs.title: Pass token via environment variable
docs.text:
confluence-markdown --action read \
  --base-url https://confluence.example.com \
  --username myuser \
  --token "$CONFLUENCE_TOKEN" \
  "https://confluence.example.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345"
